/Issued 300 PM MDT Fri Sep 25 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

This afternoon an upper-level trough, associated with a Pacific Cold 
Front, with strong southerly flow approaches Montana. Due to a 
strong surface pressure gradient and strong low-level and mid-level 
winds it will be windy this afternoon across North-central, Central, 
and Southwestern Montana. The Pacific Cold Front will move through 
the area this afternoon/evening. This will bring strong winds to the 
Rocky Mountain Front and plains west of I-15 this evening though 
early Saturday morning. As the cold front moves through North-
central Montana, rain showers have the potential to bring gusty to 
strong winds. Tonight light snow will affect the Rocky Mountain 
Front. See the Forecast Confidence & Scenarios Section for 
details. 

On Saturday the upper-level trough remains over North-central, 
Central, and Southwestern Montana. This combined with the cold front 
will bring cold temperatures (slightly below seasonal averages) to 
the area. Saturday morning snow will linger along the Rocky Mountain 
Front and it will be mostly dry elsewhere. On Sunday an upper-level 
ridge begins to build in over North-central, Central, and 
Southwestern Montana. This will keep cool temperatures over the area 
with mostly dry weather. On Monday a weak upper-level trough moves 
over the area. This will allow temperatures to warm up some with 
isolated showers around. On Tuesday an upper-level ridge briefly 
builds in over the area. This will allow warm temperatures to remain 
with dry weather. Tuesday night into Wednesday the upper-level ridge 
breaks down. This will bring strong winds to North-central Montana. 
On Wednesday and Thursday there will be zonal flow over North-
central, Central, and Southwestern Montana. This will bring breezy, 
warm, and dry conditions to the area on Wednesday and Thursday. For 
details for Friday through next weekend see the Forecast Confidence 
and Scenarios section. -IG

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Along the Rocky Mountain and plains west of I-15 there is greater 
than an 80% chance for wind gusts of 55 mph or greater this evening 
through tomorrow morning. Since hi-res models suggested that 
strong winds could last until noon tomorrow, the High Wind Warning
for those areas was extended until noon tomorrow. In the Sweet 
Grass Hills there is greater than an 80% chance for wind gusts of 
55 mph or greater from this evening through early tomorrow 
morning. However since this is a localized area a High Wind 
Warning was not issued for this area. The HREF (Hi-res ensemble 
forecast) showed strong 850 mb winds greater than 40 kts over the 
bears paw mountains associated with the cold front. As a result a 
High Wind Warning was issued for the Bears Paw Mountains from 8 PM
tonight through 6 AM tomorrow morning. 

Tonight across the golden triangle region associated with the cold 
front a line of showers will move through. At least isolated 
portions of the line have at least a low chance to produce wind 
gusts in excess of 58 mph (severe wind gusts). Tonight along the 
northern Rocky Mountain Front there is at least a 80% chance for 
greater than a tenth of an inch of snow. Tonight along the higher 
peaks of the northern Rocky Mountain Front (the eastern portion of
Glacier National Park) there is a greater than a 60% chance for 
an inch of snow.

Next Friday through next Sunday some of the models and ensembles are 
predicting a snowfall event. Two of the four clusters which 
represents around 50% of the ensemble members have an upper-level 
trough over Montana next Friday through next Sunday. This 
scenario would bring well-below seasonal averages for temperatures
with the potential for both lower-elevation and mountain snow 
next Friday through next Sunday. These two clusters differ on how
strong and how far east the upper-level trough is. A stronger 
trough centered over Montana would bring more snow and colder 
temperatures than a trough that is less strong and/or further 
east. The other two clusters which represents the other 50% of 
ensemble membership have a upper-level ridge over North-central, 
Central, and Southwestern Montana next Friday through next 
Sunday. This will bring above seasonal average temperatures with 
dry weather to the area next Friday through next Sunday. -IG
